title: story-043 'provable solvency invariant' overstated: ERC4626 double round-down means convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)) can be a few wei below creditedPrincipal
specSource: story-043 (commit a65dbf0 body) + _creditedPrincipal NatSpec lines 207-210: 'fairValueOfShares >= creditedPrincipal a provable solvency invariant'
description: minOut = convertToShares(creditedPrincipal) guarantees sharesReceived >= minOut, but because convertToShares and convertToAssets both round DOWN, convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)) can be below creditedPrincipal by sub-wei / few-wei dust. The chain therefore proves fairValue >= (a value possibly below creditedPrincipal), not >= creditedPrincipal; the 'provable' qualifier in the story-043 claim is overstated. Accumulates on flat markets.
impact: Sub-wei / few-wei rounding dust per deposit (accumulates on flat markets); no realizable asset impact. The conservative-crediting INTENT is faithfully implemented.
assumptions: ERC4626 convertToShares and convertToAssets both round down.
justification: FAITHFULNESS (Law-2) — routed to the spec-conformance report as F-01, NOT the QA/gas bundle. story-043 claims the solvency invariant is 'provable'; strictly the round-trip can dip below creditedPrincipal by ERC4626 double-round-down dust, so the 'provable' qualifier is overstated. Pure behavioural/claim deviation with negligible security impact, but surfaced visibly to the owner per Law-2 rather than dropped into noise. Conservative crediting itself conforms.
recommendation: Amend the claim to 'fairValue >= creditedPrincipal - dust', or add a small protocol-favoring epsilon to minOut so the round-trip cannot dip below creditedPrincipal.
